limitations_and_boundaries: Optimal feature embedding or network architecture for physics-informed DeepONets remains an open question.
Appropriate loss weights for training physics-informed DeepONets are not determined.
Algorithms for accelerating training and ensuring accuracy and robustness are needed.

research_questions.statement: Can physics-informed DeepONets improve predictive accuracy and data efficiency for learning solution operators of parametric PDEs?

provenance.text_excerpt: enhanced data-efficiency (up to 100% reduction in the number of examples required to train a DeepONet model)

claims.statement: Physics-informed DeepONets greatly reduce the need for large training datasets.

provenance.text_excerpt: a trained physics informed DeepOnet model can predict the solution of O(10^3) time-dependent PDEs in a fraction of a second – up to three orders of magnitude faster compared a conventional PDE solver

claims.statement: Physics-informed DeepONets achieve up to three orders of magnitude speedup over conventional PDE solvers.

provenance.text_excerpt: we observe significant improvements in predictive accuracy (up to 1-2 orders of magnitude reduction in predictive errors)

claims.statement: Physics-informed DeepONets significantly improve predictive accuracy over conventional DeepONets.

provenance.text_excerpt: physics-informed DeepONets are capable of solving parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) without any paired input-output observations, except for a set of given initial or boundary conditions

claims.statement: Physics-informed DeepONets can solve parametric PDEs without any paired input-output observations, except for initial/boundary conditions.

datasets.description: Synthetic data generated from parametric PDEs: diffusion-reaction, Burgers', advection, and Eikonal equations with varying parameters, initial/boundary conditions.
datasets.name: Parametric PDE benchmarks

experiments_or_tasks: Compare against conventional DeepONets and PDE solvers in terms of accuracy, data efficiency, and speed.
Evaluate on various parametric PDEs including diffusion-reaction, Burgers', advection, and Eikonal equations.
Propose physics-informed DeepONets that incorporate physical laws via soft penalty constraints using automatic differentiation.

methods.name: Physics-informed DeepONet
methods.protocol_description: DeepONet architecture with physics-informed loss: total loss = data loss (if available) + PDE residual loss + boundary/initial condition loss. PDE residual computed via automatic differentiation. Trained with Adam optimizer.

methods.name: Conventional DeepONet
methods.protocol_description: Standard DeepONet trained solely on paired input-output data without physics constraints.
